response.sql: WITH event_ratio AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, SUM(spent) / NULLIF(SUM(amount), 0) AS spend_ratio FROM budget WHERE link_to_event IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_event), avg_ratio AS (SELECT AVG(spend_ratio) AS avg_spend_ratio FROM event_ratio) SELECT e.event_id, e.spend_ratio, e.spend_ratio / a.avg_spend_ratio AS relative_spend_ratio FROM event_ratio e CROSS JOIN avg_ratio a ORDER BY relative_spend_ratio IS NULL, relative_spend_ratio DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The database is SQLite, so SUM and AVG skip NULLs, NULLIF(...,0) turns a zero or NULL amount total into NULL, and ORDER BY relative_spend_ratio IS NULL places missing ratios last in a descending sort.
Budget lines with a NULL link_to_event are not attributed to any event and are excluded.
An event whose total amount is 0 or missing has no defined spend ratio; it is excluded from the overall average and sorts last.
The overall average is the plain mean of the per-event ratios (each event counts once), not a total-spent over total-amount figure.
Ties in relative_spend_ratio have no defined order, so which tied events make the top 10 is not fixed.

alternatives.interpretation: If the database is not SQLite and supports NULLS LAST (for example PostgreSQL), the missing-last ordering can be written directly instead of with the IS NULL trick.
alternatives.sql: WITH event_ratio AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, SUM(spent) / NULLIF(SUM(amount), 0) AS spend_ratio FROM budget WHERE link_to_event IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_event), avg_ratio AS (SELECT AVG(spend_ratio) AS avg_spend_ratio FROM event_ratio) SELECT e.event_id, e.spend_ratio, e.spend_ratio / a.avg_spend_ratio AS relative_spend_ratio FROM event_ratio e CROSS JOIN avg_ratio a ORDER BY relative_spend_ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
